messages:
maria: Quick FYI — noticed a ~6.5% drop in prefix cache hit-rate on prod for chat flows after the tokenizer bump last night.
ken: which tokenizer bump? the shared tokenizer lib or model-specific tokenization change? :thinking_face: 
maria: shared-tokenizer v2.4.0 (lib update). perf-bot: summary attached from the 1h window after deploy: hit-rate 82% -> 76%, P50 latency +4ms on cached requests.
sam: interesting — could be because cache keying started including token ids instead of raw text? any diffs in canonicalization?
maria: that's my suspicion. The deploy included a change that normalizes whitespace via tokenizer.encode(join) which can reorder some unicode normalizations vs old path. I ran a quick diff of keys and saw many near-duplicates with tiny pre-token differences.
ken: We need a deterministic "prompt signature" tie-breaker. Proposal: cache key = SHA256( canonical_prompt + "|" + tokenizer_version + "|" + system_prompt_hash + "|" + sorted_tools_blob ). Exclude ephemeral fields like trace_id, timestamp, user_device_id.
anjali: +1. Also we should canonicalize embedded JSON arguments by lexicographically sorting object keys and removing whitespace. Example: ```{"user": "a", "meta": {"b":1}} -> {"meta":{"b":1},"user":"a"}``` This will avoid tool-arg order regressions.
sam: fine, but watch out for kernel selection/batching changes: if canonicalization increases average token length for common prefixes, kernel selector might pick a different execution kernel and that could bump latency or OOMs. We should simulate kernel-choice impact in perf harness before flip.
perf-bot: perf-check results (canary): applying canonical signature reduced unique cache keys by 4.8% in a 10k-sample trace, estimated hit-rate +3.6%. Kernel selector delta: negligible for ~95% of traces; 5% switched to slower fp16 path causing mean +6ms.
maria: ok — action plan: 1) implement signature PR that pins tokenizer_version string into key, 2) add normalization step for tool args (sorted keys), 3) add canary job that measures both hit-rate and kernel-selection changes, 4) add a rollback toggle in config.
ken: also add telemetry for "cache_key_version" tag so we can backfill and compare historical counts.
anjali: on warmup: we should send golden prefixes to warmup pool keyed by new signature to avoid cold-miss spike. Maybe use rolling warmup for 24h post-deploy.
sam: +1. And for batching heuristics, consider keeping small-request grouping separate for warmup so we don't inflate batch sizes and change batching latency profile.
maria: I'll draft the PR with the canonicalization rules and a feature flag (cache_key_v3). Can someone own the canary job config?
ken: I can set up the canary in staging and mirror a percentage of prod traffic. Will add kernel-selection probes.
anjali: I'll add the warmup job and a small prompt set for chat flows.
perf-bot: noted. I will emit a follow-up report 2h after canary start with hit-rate and kernel-switch metrics.
maria: thanks everyone. If we see >3% latency regressions in cached path we rollback. Otherwise roll forward after 24h. :thumbsup:
__notes: Slack thread: cache keying -> tokenizer pinning -> canonicalization tie-breaker; includes perf bot numbers and concrete action items.
